input.content:
Listing all running services on the system...

Note: This file contains service status information. To get the actual service status,
you would typically run one of these commands on a Linux system:

1. systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   - Lists all services with their status (active, inactive, failed, etc.)

2. systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
   - Lists only running services

3. service --status-all
   - Shows status of all services (older systems)

4. ps aux
   - Shows all running processes

5. systemctl status
   - Shows overall system status

Example output format:
UNIT                                   LOAD   ACTIVE SUB       DESCRIPTION
accounts-daemon.service                loaded active running   Accounts Service
acpid.service                           loaded active running   ACPI Event Daemon
alsa-restore.service                    loaded active exited    Save and restore the mixer state
alsa-state.service                      loaded active running   Manage Sound Card State (restore and store)
...

To view the actual running services on your system, execute:
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running

This will show all currently active and running services with their status.

RUNNING SERVICES STATUS REPORT
================================

This report contains information about system services and their status.

To list all running services on a Linux system, use one of these commands:

1. SYSTEMCTL (Modern Linux systems):
   systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
   
   This shows:
   - UNIT: Service name
   - LOAD: Whether the unit definition was properly loaded
   - ACTIVE: Whether the unit is currently active
   - SUB: Lower-level unit activation state
   - DESCRIPTION: Human-readable description

2. SERVICE COMMAND (Older systems):
   service --status-all
   
   Shows [ + ] for running services and [ - ] for stopped services

3. PROCESS STATUS:
   ps aux | grep -E "^[^ ]+ +[0-9]+ +0 " (shows root processes)
   
4. SYSTEMD STATUS:
   systemctl status
   
   Shows overall system status and key services

COMMON RUNNING SERVICES TYPICALLY FOUND:
- sshd: SSH server for remote access
- systemd-journald: System logging service
- systemd-logind: Login session manager
- dbus: System message bus
- NetworkManager or networking: Network connectivity
- cron or crond: Task scheduler
- rsyslog or journald: System logging
- udev: Device manager
- systemd-resolved: DNS resolver
- multipathd: Multipath device mapper
- polkit: Authorization service
- avahi-daemon: mDNS/DNS-SD service
- cups: Print service
- docker: Container runtime (if installed)
- postgresql/mysql: Database services (if installed)
- nginx/apache2: Web servers (if installed)

To get the actual list on your system, run:
systemctl list-units --type=service --all --no-pager

Or for just running services:
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager
